facts.text: Tb was added to produce (VNb)0.67(TiTbHf)0.33, which was directly compared with the Tb-free (VNb)0.753(TiHf)0.247 alloy.
Both compared alloys were arc-melted under Ti-gettered Ar and remelted five times.
Field-dependent heat-capacity transitions were measured down to 1.8 K in fields up to about 5–6 T, and the upper critical fields were derived with the dirty-limit WHH model.
The Tb-containing bcc matrix had a lattice parameter of 3.2642(1) Å, compared with 3.2568(1) Å for the Tb-free matrix, indicating some Tb incorporation.
The Tb-containing alloy contained 2.9 wt.% pure-Tb precipitates and 1.7 wt.% Tb2O3 in addition to its bcc HEA matrix.
The Tb and Tb2O3 inclusions acted mainly as nonsuperconducting regions that reduced the effective superconducting volume, rather than as effective flux-pinning centers.
Adding Tb lowered the superconducting transition temperature and broadened the superconducting transition relative to the Tb-free alloy.
The heat-capacity transition temperature was 4.6(1) K for the Tb-containing alloy versus 5.2(1) K for the Tb-free alloy.
Adding Tb reduced the zero-temperature upper critical field relative to the Tb-free alloy.
The WHH-derived μ0Hc2(0) was 6.1 T for the Tb-containing alloy versus 6.8 T for the Tb-free alloy.
At an applied field of 5 T, the Tb-free alloy remained superconducting whereas the Tb-containing alloy was paramagnetic.
The normalized heat-capacity jump decreased from 1.49 in the Tb-free alloy to 1.05 in the Tb-containing alloy.
